BiblicalUsage: Chashah is keeping quiet, holding one's peace, and it is a silence that can be wisdom or cowardice. The king of Israel asks why they sit still and take not Ramoth from the king of Syria, the sons of the prophets tell Elisha to hold his peace because his master will be taken, the Preacher says there is a time to keep silence and a time to speak, and God says He has long time holden His peace and been still.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe silence in Scripture is never empty: a king's stillness loses a city, a prophet's stillness guards a grief, and God's stillness is patience before He cries like a travailing woman. I hold that knowing when to keep silence is a gift, and the Preacher is right that it has its time.
